stories.headline: Columbus Crew 2 fires Higuain after fallout from ref abuse
stories.summary: The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.
stories.body:
The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.

"We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuaín from his responsibilities," said Crew General Manager Issa Tall in prepared statement. "After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met," The Crew's statement added that for the 2026 MLS NEXT Pro Playoffs, the Crew 2 technical staff will assume additional responsibilities ahead of the Club's search for a full-time head coach for the side.

Higuain, 41, was suspended for two games following an Aug. 23 incident that involved him refusing to let go of the hand of a female referee during the post-game handshake, despite being asked three times to do so. Higuain also directed a sexist remark toward the referee saying: "Don't forget that this is a man's game."

Higuain, who excelled as a player for the Crew over eight seasons, was red carded for the incident. In addition to the two-game suspension, Higuain was ordered to undergo restorative practice training, sources told ESPN.

An MLS NEXT Pro spokesperson confirmed that Higuain was suspended for just one additional game, as the policy allows for the red card to count towards the total suspension. The same spokesperson wasn't able to answer the question of why Higuain's actions didn't constitute a forceful grab.

The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), the union that represents MLS and USL referees, brought the incident to light over the weekend, stating in a social media post that it was not satisfied with the penalties, adding that a "forceful grab" plus the discriminatory language should have been penalized more severely.

While the PSRA's post didn't mention Higuain by name, ESPN reported that the coach in question was Higuain.

"The League's response falls drastically short of the right message to the participants, the referees, and the public. It needs to be reevaluated," the PSRA's social media post read.

The Crew initially issued a statement stating that, "The Crew actively collaborated with MLS NEXT Pro throughout the review process and fully accepted the additional discipline issued in accordance with league policies.

"We condemn any action or notion that contradicts our mission of uniting and uplifting all communities and genders through the global game."

But sources with knowledge of the Crew's decision to fire its coach told ESPN that the club wasn't satisfied with Higuain's response to the incident, saying there was a "lack of contrition" on his part, that he refused to issue a public apology to the female referee, and that there was an overall lack of accountability on the part of its second-team coach.

There was pressure from several of the Crew's supporters groups as well, including the Nordecke and CapyBrava, which both made social media posts demanding that Higuain be fired.

One source said that Higuain was informed of the club's decision early Tuesday afternoon.

In a statement given to ESPN on Sunday, MLS NEXT Pro said the league "immediately investigated the reported incident between the head coach and the female official. It was determined that the coach's behavior violated League policies and warranted additional discipline beyond the red card that was issued in the moment. He served a two-game suspension and is required to participate in a multi-session restorative practices process, which is already underway. The program is intended to support the League's efforts to foster understanding, accountability, respect, and the restoration of relationships across the League. MLS NEXT Pro believes in the restorative approach. The League is confident in its process and the results."

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Walker's on but Woolf 'wouldn't swap' his own No.7
stories.summary: Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has shown the skill and mindset to win big games and coach Kristian Woolf backs him to the hilt for their preliminary final.
stories.body:
All the hype has been around the early return of Sydney Roosters halfback Sam Walker from injury but Dolphins coach Kristian Woolf has full faith his own No.7 has the skillset to shine in his biggest test yet.

Dolphins co-captain Isaiya Katoa, 22, will be integral to a win in the grand final qualifier against the Roosters at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night.

Katoa has 18 try assists this year in 21 games. Walker has 21 in the same number of matches.

In linebreak involvements Katoa is second best in the NRL behind only Cody Walker, boasting 31 this year. Sam Walker has nine for the season.

It is Katoa's cool, calm and collected ability to make others around him better with subtle touches that sets him apart and makes him such a danger to the opposition and a weapon for his team.

Woolf said he expected Walker, back from a four-week layoff with an ankle injury, to line up for the Roosters and bring "a bit of the unknown" to the game but is just glad the Dolphins have Katoa.

"I certainly wouldn't swap Isaiya for anyone," Woolf said.

"I love what he brings as a person and how he carries himself and he plays with that same calmness and confidence that he has got in himself.

"I am looking forward to what he can do tomorrow night."

Katoa played with maturity in his first final experience, the 26-16 win in the away qualifying final against the Warriors after the Dolphins trailed 16-8.

"What impressed me was that he kept his cool regardless of the score and a hostile crowd that did influence some decisions," Woolf said.

"It really impressed me how he turned the game in the second half with kicking. It was a 10 out of 10 (performance) and allowed us to put the Warriors under pressure."

Woolf's message to all his players has been to "enjoy the week" and back the toughness and skill that has got them this far.

Founding Dolphins forwards Jesse and Kenny Bromwich and Mark Nicholls spoke to the group on Thursday before their captain's run.

Woolf said the retired trio had "set a tone for what we want our culture to be and what sort of men we want representing the club".

"It was important for them to come in and brush shoulders with the players ... and the players loved seeing them," Woolf said.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson has big game experience with three NRL titles to his credit.

Woolf, however, knows about finals footy better than most after taking St Helens to three Super League titles and a Challenge Cup final victory.

Dolphins lock Morgan Knowles played in those wins under Woolf at St Helens.

"He's pretty consistent with his messages but once he gets to this time of the year, less is more," Knowles told AAP.

"I remember the grand final in 2020 against Wigan back in the UK he only showed us one video clip all week.

"It was when we previously played them in the year and they had a bit of a carry-on and were trying to impose themselves on us. That is all he needed to show."

The players were fired up enough to not leave anything in the tank.

"In the big games it comes down to the little moments when you are willing to keep turning up, put your body on the line and make the plays that don't get noticed," Knowles said.

The Dolphins beat the Roosters 26-12 in round 26 when Woolf's men defended their line with grit.

It was the template for a style the coach said had been a strength ever since they were flogged 66-0 by Cronulla in round 19. Since then the Dolphins have won eight straight and averaged 16.75 points against per match.

stories.headline: NBA Rank 2026: The new top 10 features a razor-thin race for No. 1
stories.summary: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players hits its grand finale.
stories.body:
Welcome to the grand finale of NBA Rank 2026.

After unveiling Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday and Nos. 50-11 on Wednesday, the big reveal is here.

Who will be the top 10 players for the 2026-27 season? How high did reigning Finals MVP Jalen Brunson climb? Did Victor Wembanyama just begin a LeBron James-esque run atop of the list?

While ESPN's latest top 10 -- err, full top 100 -- will surely spark debate, what can't be questioned is the remarkably tight race for this season's No. 1 spot. Just three voting points separated Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Wembanyama, with each superstar placing atop at least one of the seven panelists' individual rankings.

That panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition. In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven NBA experts: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list -- the best of the best heading into the new NBA season.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

10. Donovan Mitchell
G | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 15

Mitchell rises into the top 10 after leading the Cavaliers to the Eastern Conference finals last season, his first such appearance in his nine-year career. He has finished in the top seven in MVP voting in three of the past four seasons, and his ability to create off the dribble while using his shooting range to freeze defenders makes him the offensive force of the Cavs. Mitchell has been an All-Star in seven straight seasons, and he pairs with James Harden to give Cleveland one of the few backcourts where each starter boasts multiple All-NBA selections.

Biggest question: Can Mitchell be the best player on a champion?

The Cavaliers start four All-Stars in Mitchell, Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, but in the playoffs they will only go as far as Mitchell can lead them.

One of the ironies of Mitchell's first run to the conference finals was that he didn't play particularly well compared to past postseasons. In his six playoffs runs from 2020 to 2025, Mitchell averaged 30.0 points per game with a Player Efficiency Rating (PER) of 24.5. Last season, he averaged 26.0 points with a PER of just 18.6 (15.0 is considered average). The former version is absolutely good enough to carry the Cavs back to the Finals, especially if Mitchell sees a repeat performance from his teammates. -- André Snellings

Signature stat: Mitchell is one of eight players to average at least 20 points per game in each of the past nine seasons.

Fantasy projection: 26.8 PTS, 5.7 AST, 4.8 REB, 1.6 STL

9. Jayson Tatum
F | Boston Celtics

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

Tatum wasn't eligible for NBA Rank last fall because of an Achilles tendon tear he sustained in May 2025, and the two other notable players who tore an Achilles tendon around the same time -- Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard -- both sat out the entire campaign. But Tatum returned after a concerted and relatively speedy recovery, and in his 16 regular-season and six playoff games, he was remarkably productive for someone who had suffered such a devastating injury less than 12 months prior.

Tatum did miss Game 7 of the Celtics' playoff loss to Philadelphia because of a mysterious injury, but he'll end up having had another six months of recovery time by opening night this season. He might look even more like his former self -- and he'll need to be after the Celtics traded co-star Jaylen Brown to the 76ers in the offseason.

Big question: Is Tatum's ceiling still as high post-injury?

Tatum was good in his limited playing time last season. But he was far more than merely good before his Achilles tear. For four consecutive seasons prior to the injury, Tatum was a first-team All-NBA selection, which is the level that most championship teams need from their No. 1 options. If Tatum can't return to that level, the Celtics likely won't have enough top-tier star power to return to the Finals. But if Tatum returns to MVP contender status, Boston will be right back in the title mix. -- Zach Kram

Signature stat: Tatum is one of three players to average at least 25 points, eight rebounds and five assists per game across the past two seasons, joining Nikola Jokic and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

Fantasy projection: 26.7 PTS, 8.6 REB, 5.8 AST, 1.1 STL

8. Cade Cunningham
G | Detroit Pistons

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 12

Cunningham vaulted into top 10 thanks to a spectacular 2025-26 season in which he earned first-team All-NBA honors and led the Pistons to the franchise's first 60-win season in 20 years. The No. 1 draft pick in 2021 has successfully weathered early-career injuries and a miserable 14-win campaign in 2023-24 to emerge as an elite playmaker. Cunningham excels at controlling game flow, manipulating matchups and changing speeds, and he has lived up to hopeful predraft assessments that viewed him in the same mold as James Harden and Luka Doncic. With Cunningham turning 25 on Friday, the Pistons must focus solely on maximizing the talent around him over the next three to five seasons. His and Detroit's window of opportunity is now.

Big question for 2026-27: Will Cunningham solve his turnover problems?

High-usage playmakers are bound to turn the ball over, especially when they're asked to log huge minutes in the playoffs. But Cunningham set an unfortunate record during the 2026 postseason: Detroit's franchise guard averaged 5.6 turnovers per game, the most by any player in NBA history during a playoff run of at least 10 games.

Cunningham can be sloppy with the ball, but Detroit's cramped spacing and lack of secondary ball handlers make his job much more difficult. Even though the Pistons have gradually improved their cast of outside shooters by adding Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe since the 2025 offseason, they're destined for more playoff heartbreak unless they find another star-level creator to properly balance their offense. For proof of concept, the Pistons should look back at the 2018 Rockets' pairing of James Harden and Chris Paul and the 2024 Mavericks' duo of Luka Doncic and Kyrie Irving. Thanks to the multipronged attacks during those seasons, Houston won 65 games and Dallas made a stunning trip to the Finals. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Last season, Cunningham became the first Piston to score 1,500 points in consecutive campaigns since Jerry Stackhouse's three straight from 1999-2000 to 2001-02.

Fantasy projection: 24.6 PTS, 9.8 AST, 5.6 REB, 1.4 STL

7. Anthony Edwards
G | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 6

Still only 25, Edwards grabbed the mantle of best two-way wing in the NBA during Jayson Tatum's injury absence last season. Edwards averaged a career-high 28.8 points per game and again made 40% of his 3s on high volume (as he did in 2024-25) while enjoying his most efficient season overall. And while Edwards missed out on an All-NBA nod because he appeared in only 61 games, he is generally one of the sturdiest stars around, having appeared in at least 72 games in each of his previous five campaigns.

Big question: Can Edwards continue to improve as a facilitator?

With only one exception -- a certain French center -- the players ranked ahead of Edwards on this list and the league's leading MVP candidates are so effective because they create prime scoring opportunities for both themselves and their teammates. But Edwards doesn't quite yet fit that expansive playmaking role, even as he improves every year with his reads out of pick-and-rolls.

The Timberwolves' experiment of using Edwards as a point guard appears to be over after trading for LaMelo Ball this offseason. But that might not get in the way of Edwards' development in this capacity; last season, he posted his lowest assist rate since he was a rookie. -- Kram

Signature stat: Edwards' 10,854 career points are the third most in NBA history before turning 25, trailing LeBron James (13,927) and Kevin Durant (12,258).

Fantasy projection: 30.3 PTS, 5.2 REB, 4.0 AST, 1.3 STL

6. Jalen Brunson
G | New York Knicks

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 10

The "King of New York" became the king of the NBA in June, powering the Knicks to their first title in over 50 years. He earned All-NBA honors for the third straight year and was named conference finals MVP and Finals MVP -- all while shutting down every critique about his size at 6-foot-2 and 190 pounds. Brunson is cemented into Knicks lore as an all-time great. A parity-busting repeat would put him on the doorstep of all-time great status leaguewide.

Biggest question: Can Brunson keep the Knicks focused in an improved East?

It will be said ad nauseam this season: There hasn't been a repeat champion since the Golden State Warriors in 2017 and 2018, when Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant were co-supernovas.

Every champion since has had a hiccup on the way to June. The Eastern Conference is as deep as it has been in decades, and the Knicks are now the biggest target. It won't just be when teams come into Madison Square Garden; the Knicks will be everyone's biggest game. That requires extra stamina. It's also the time when a collective group can splinter and begin thinking about contracts rather than sacrifice.

The captain will have to keep this group on task for the better part of six months -- then ramp it up again for the playoffs. So much laid out perfectly after an up-and-down 2025-26 regular season, and the Knicks often cleared the way for Brunson to take over in the fourth quarters of games. Can the Knicks deploy the same formula? Or will Brunson have to make statistical sacrifices to keep everybody onboard until the playoffs begin? His leadership will be tested. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Brunson averaged 11.2 fourth-quarter points during the 2026 NBA Finals, the most ever by a guard and second to only Shaquille O'Neal in 1995 and 2000.

Fantasy projection: 26.9 PTS, 6.9 AST, 3.3 REB, 0.9 STL

5. Giannis Antetokounmpo
F | Miami Heat

Age: 31

2025 NBA Rank: 4

Antetokounmpo continued to put up MVP-caliber numbers last season but didn't finish in the top four of the MVP vote for the first time in eight years because he missed so much time due to injury. The 31-year-old forward played just 36 games in his final season with the Bucks, and he will enter his first with the Heat needing to prove he is still in his prime and can stay healthy. If both are true in 2026-27, Antetokounmpo will remain one of the very few players capable of averaging 30 points and 10 rebounds while also leading his team in assists.

Big question for 2026-27: Can Antetokounmpo lead the Heat into championship contention in Year 1?

When the Heat traded away a large collection of players and draft assets to bring in Antetokounmpo, the general consensus was that it would take multiple seasons to reopen Miami's title window. But why not now? The Heat made it to at least the conference finals three times in four campaigns from 2020 to 2023 with a team built around Jimmy Butler III and Bam Adebayo, with role players at every other key position.

"Heat Culture" is real, implemented by team president Pat Riley and coach Erik Spoelstra, which means Miami is always defensive-minded and edgy. The Heat tend to squeeze every ounce of potential out of their lineups and garner more success than general expectations on a yearly basis. Enter Antetokounmpo, who gives them the most talented player since LeBron James led Miami to four consecutive Finals and back-to-back titles almost 15 years ago.

Antetokounmpo's ability to be a one-man wrecking ball and offense creator at one end while crashing boards and playing disruptive defense at the other end might still be unmatched. Opponents will still have to "build the wall" to keep him from dominating the paint, which means teammates will continue to feast on open looks when Antetokounmpo drives -- and the Heat added Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. to capitalize. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Antetokounmpo left Milwaukee as one of four players to lead an active franchise in points, rebounds and assists, joining LeBron James with Cleveland, Kevin Garnett with Minnesota and Michael Jordan with Chicago.

Fantasy projection: 32.1 PTS, 11.4 REB, 6.3 AST, 1.1 STL

4. Luka Doncic
G | Los Angeles Lakers

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 3

Coming off his second scoring title in the past three years (33.48 points per game) and continuing to sport the revamped physique he committed to in the summer of 2025, Doncic is primed for another dominant season quarterbacking the Lakers. The 6-foot-8 star's fingerprints were all over L.A.'s roster construction over the offseason, as the front office heeded his desire for an "A-list center" by trading for Walker Kessler and opened up the team's coffers to retain Doncic's dynamic backcourt partner, Austin Reaves. Now 27, Doncic is entering what traditionally has been identified as the start of a player's prime -- although he is arguably already there, as evidenced by his six All-NBA selections since joining the NBA in 2018.

Big question for 2026-27: Can Doncic win with this group?

Through two postseasons with the Lakers, Doncic has been on the court for only one playoff win. That's it. In 2025, L.A. was the Western Conference's No. 3 seed and got upset by the sixth-seeded Timberwolves in five games. This past spring, the Lakers made it to the conference semifinals as the 4-seed, but Doncic was sidelined for both rounds because of a hamstring issue.

Doncic's trips with the Dallas Mavericks to the West finals in 2022 and the NBA Finals in 2024 are starting to feel like distant history. And since his Finals loss to the Celtics in 2024, Doncic has been passed in career accomplishments by some of his contemporaries -- with the 28-year-old Shai Gilgeous-Alexander winning back-to-back MVPs and an NBA title and Doncic's former teammate Jalen Brunson, 30, leading the Knicks to their first championship in more than 50 years.

Is Doncic equipped to compete with the likes of Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder -- the team that swept L.A. out of the second round without him -- and Victor Wembanyama's Spurs? -- Dave McMenamin

Signature stat: Doncic is one of three players with 15,000 points, 4,000 rebounds and 4,000 assists in their first eight NBA seasons, joining LeBron James and Oscar Robertson.

Fantasy projection: 33.0 PTS, 8.9 AST, 8.5 REB, 1.6 STL

3. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
G | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 2

Not returning to the NBA Finals should only motivate the reigning back-to-back MVP. But as the loss to the Spurs in the Western Conference finals proved, the Thunder are at their best when Gilgeous-Alexander has a healthy Jalen Williams paired with him. In the minutes they shared the court, Oklahoma City outscored its opponents by 15.3 points per 100 possessions. Besides trying to get back to the Finals, Gilgeous-Alexander is attempting to become the third guard to shoot better than 50% from the field in five straight seasons. Only Hall of Famers Magic Johnson and Maurice Cheeks have done it.

Biggest question for 2026-27: Can Gilgeous-Alexander become the first player since 1986 to win three straight MVPs?

Even with the dominant runs of Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant, Shaquille O'Neal, Tim Duncan, LeBron James, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokic, no player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. Gilgeous-Alexander enters the 2026-27 season behind Victor Wembanyama in MVP odds, according to DraftKings. -- Bobby Marks

Signature stat: This season, Gilgeous-Alexander can join Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan on the list of players to average 30 points on 50% shooting for at least five campaigns in a row.

Fantasy projection: 31.3 PTS, 6.4 AST, 4.9 REB, 1.7 STL

2. Victor Wembanyama
C | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 22

2025 NBA Rank: 5

If not for a series of Spurs collapses in the NBA Finals, basketball fans everywhere would have crowned Wembanyama "Best Player in the World" in June. Instead, the 22-year-old center will enter his fourth season seeking championship validation and his first MVP award to go with the Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-NBA honors he earned last season. "The Alien" continues to ace the eye test and advanced stats alike, and he boosted his scoring efficiency in 2025-26 by cutting back on his 3-point attempts in favor of paint opportunities. After leading the league in blocks and defensive win shares during the regular season, Wembanyama posted an excellent plus-12.9 net rating during his first playoff run. What's scarier for opponents: His 7-foot-4 (7-5? 7-6?) frame or his rapid rate of improvement?

Big question for 2026-27: What did Wembanyama learn from his NBA Finals defeat?

No matter how much time passes, the 2026 Finals' "tortoise and hare" dynamic still seems unfathomable. San Antonio outscored New York by 57 points in the first quarters of their five-game series only to then be outscored by 29 points in the second quarters, by 14 points in the third quarters and by 26 points in the fourth quarters. Wembanyama & Co. simply couldn't protect their leads.

While the Spurs' collective youth came back to bite them on the biggest stage, Wembanyama appeared to display physical and mental fatigue during his team's second-half struggles. What's more, he rightfully praised Knicks guard Jalen Brunson for dictating the late-game action.

To claim his first title, Wembanyama must improve his stamina and avoid an overreliance on isolation jumpers when playoff games tighten. Throughout its history, San Antonio has always won as a team. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Last season, Wembanyama became the NBA's first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year, an award first presented in 1983.

Fantasy projection: 26.3 PTS, 12.2 REB, 3.5 AST, 3.5 BLK

1. Nikola Jokic
C | Denver Nuggets

Age: 31

2025 NBA Rank: 1

The margin between Jokic, Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was razor-thin for the top spot in ESPN's NBA Rank. All three players deserved the No. 1 slot, but it's Jokic in the first position for the third consecutive year. In 2025-26, he averaged a triple-double for the second straight season, joining Russell Westbrook as the only players to accomplish the feat multiple times. Although Jokic finished second in MVP voting once again, he has either won the award or been runner-up across six consecutive campaigns.

Big question for 2026-27: Will Jokic's 3-point shooting return to form?

There will be questions around the Nuggets' depth after losing Peyton Watson this offseason. There will be questions about Jokic's next contract, despite him saying, "My desire is to play the rest of my life in Denver." But from an on-court perspective, his 3-point shooting dipped considerably after he suffered a bone bruise in his hyperextended left knee on Dec. 29, causing him to miss 16 games. Prior to the injury, Jokic was shooting 44% from deep, which would have been a career high. That rate dropped to 32% from when he returned in late January until the end of the regular season.

Those struggles continued against the Timberwolves in the first round of the playoffs, during which he shot 7-for-36 (19.4%) from beyond the arc for the sixth-worst percentage in postseason history among players with at least 35 attempts. In a Western Conference with defensive rim protectors such as Wembanyama, Rudy Gobert and Walker Kessler, Jokic's outside shooting will be key to the Nuggets' spacing. -- Matt Williams

Signature stat: Last season, Jokic became the first player in NBA history to lead the league in rebounds and assists per game.

Fantasy projection: 28.3 PTS, 12.7 REB, 10.1 AST, 1.6 STL

stories.headline: Ben Rice tops Aaron Boone's preseason prediction, passes 40 HRs
stories.summary: Yankees manager Aaron Boone predicted during spring training that Ben Rice would finish with 39 home runs this season. Rice is two-up after hitting Nos. 40 and 41 in a 9-2 victory over the Rays, tying for the AL home run lead.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Ben Rice one-upped Aaron Boone. And then he two-upped the Yankees manager.

Boone predicted during spring training that Rice would finish with 39 home runs this season. Rice hit Nos. 40 and 41 in Wednesday night's 9-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays, tying for the American League home run lead.

He smiled and pointed at Boone when he returned to the dugout after driving Mason Englert's first pitch of the game into Yankee Stadium's right-field second deck. Rice grinned at Boone some more after another solo homer in the fourth.

"I think I said, 'Hey, there's 40 for you,'" Rice recalled. "I was joking with him after the 41st one, saying, 'Hey, thanks for inspiring me this year.' But it's all in good fun. Back in spring when he told me that, I knew that secretly meant he was hoping I'd hit 40."

Rice is tied for the AL home run lead with Baltimore's Pete Alonso, Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero and Houston's Yordan Alvarez. He is hitting .263 and leads the Yankees with 97 RBIs and a .900 OPS, becoming a first-time All-Star and the biggest cog in an offense missing Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton for most of the season.

Boone deliberately picked an odd total rather than a round figure.

"I was confident he was going to have a really big year," he said. "Probably wanted to make sure it was just south of a number, maybe to maybe let him know that."

Rice, who had three hits and a walk, became the 13th Yankees player with a 40-home run season but just the third to reach the milestone during his first three seasons after Joe DiMaggio and Judge. Rice's plate appearances often prompt a rendition of Elton John's "Bennie and the Jets″ from the stadium's organist, and Rice has sparked an often struggling offense with 16 go-ahead homers this year and three that have tied games.

"One thing I always tell guys, the difference between minor leaguers and big leaguers is the consistency," Judge said. "He's one of the best. I can look up at the clock and I know exactly where he's going to be in the cage. you know what he's doing in the training room, the weight room. It's just every single day, man. This guy's a machine."

A 12th-round pick in the 2021 amateur draft from Dartmouth, where he played just 30 games over three years due to the coronavirus pandemic, Rice was mostly a catcher but occasionally a first baseman in the minors. He made his big league debut in June 2024 at age 25 after Anthony Rizzo broke a forearm.

Rice hit .171 with seven homers and 23 RBIs in 50 games that year then batted .255 with 26 homers and 65 RBIs in 138 games last year.

With Stanton sidelined for most of the season, the left-handed-hitting Rice has 93 games at designated hitter this year and 52 at first.

"It's tough to pull him off his back leg," Yankees pitcher Gerrit Cole said. "He's really able to stay balanced and deliver high-efficacy strikes on various pitches in all parts of the zone."

Rice was hitting .306 through May then batted .196 in June. An 18-for-58 (.119) slide after the All-Star break dropped his season average to .248 on Aug. 22, but he has rebounded to bat .333 (34-for-102) since.

"Went through a lull, which is inevitable, even in a great season," Boone said. "Had a stretch in there where it was a struggle and he was grinding but kind of battled through that and feel like the last few weeks has been on a really good run."

Rice's potential was evident on July 6, 2024, less than a month into his big league career, when he became the first Yankees rookie with three home runs in a game and tied Lou Gehrig's Yankees rookie record with seven RBIs. Consistency took time.

"A lot of it I always feel like is just experience-based," Rice said. "You just see more pitching at the big league level, get exposed to guys who throw all different kinds of pitches from different angles and slots and all these things. I feel like I've always been a good learner in that way."

stories.headline: Jaspa Fletcher outlines Lachie Neale legacy ahead of crucial call
stories.summary: Jaspa Fletcher will line up for his fourth AFL grand final in as many seasons aware he may never run out alongside Lachie Neale again.
stories.body:
Jaspa Fletcher has spelt out the impact Lachie Neale has made at the club as he grapples with the prospect of never playing alongside him for the Brisbane Lions again.

The 22-year-old will contest a fourth AFL grand final in his fourth season when the Lions face Fremantle on Saturday at the MCG.

As it stands Neale won't join him, the star midfielder on Thursday set to appeal a one-match suspension for striking that has ruled him out of the club's tilt for a third-straight title.

Two-time Brownlow Medallist Neale is widely tipped to join Collingwood next season.

"That's footy and that's business, and he's got to do what's right for him," Fletcher said of the former captain's likely move.

"But I'd love to still have him here, because as a mate and as a mentor as well, I can't thank him enough for what he's done for me.

"He's left such a great legacy at the club. I'm sure we'll keep a great connection over the journey."

Neale rates Fletcher, endorsing him among a host of capable young Lions leaders as a potential future captain.

"When I heard that, I was super honoured," Fletcher said.

"If that's the way the club wants to go, I'd be more than happy to do it.

"I'd do anything for the club."

Fletcher hasn't missed a game since his 2023 debut but admits his form, after preseason shoulder surgery, hadn't met his own expectations.

"I've been pretty honest ... I haven't been overly proud with how I've gone about it," he said.

"I could have got a little bit more out of myself, but that's behind me now and I've learnt a lot of lessons along the road, on and off the field."

And, after losing the only junior football grand final he reached "by 100 points", he hasn't taken his AFL career for granted.

"I'm just a product of being part of such a great club as such a great time," he said.

"In '23 we couldn't get it done, so to win a couple now is awesome. In 2023 you learn about how to go about the day, the week.

"As much as you want to win that, it set us up."

stories.headline: UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped
stories.summary: A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.
stories.body:
A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.

The Prime Minister said it was unfair for football fans to be singled out when supporters of other sports were able to drink while watching their teams.

The ban was put in place during the 1980s when concerns about hooliganism were at their height and covers the top-five tiers of English men's football.

But Everton fan Mr. Burnham said it was a measure from "an era when football was very different."

The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) welcomed the Prime Minister's words and said successful pilots of alcohol in the stands had been carried out in the women's game.

But police chiefs warned it would be "incredibly rash" to make changes without proper consultation with forces.

Mr. Burnham told reporters: "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point.

"I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.

"And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis.

"But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently from others."

The Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol) Act 1985 prohibits drinking in sight of the pitch in England and Wales in the top-five men's leagues.

FSA chairman Tom Greatrex said: "The FSA has always argued that it's unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match -- especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league.

"Many clubs are in favour as well. WSL and WSL2 ran a successful pilot, meaning fans can now drink in the stands at many grounds, while the EFL has long supported a trial.

"We welcome the Prime Minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed. We look forward to being part of that consultation."

A UK Football Policing Unit spokesman said police chiefs would welcome a meeting with Mr. Burnham to "explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans."

The spokesman said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour.

"It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games.

"Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor Report for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster.

"It would be incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence and meaningful consultation with police practitioners who have the expertise in this area."

Mr. Burnham previously raised the issue shortly before entering No. 10 in July, when rugby league fans were able to drink while watching matches at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium.

He was at the ground with friends, including Liverpool metro mayor Steve Rotheram, who were holding pints of beer, and said: "How come these lads can do that in my seat here when we can't do that at an Everton home game?

"Something wrong there. I think we need to look at that."

Saturday, September 26

Azerbaijan Grand Prix: 12 p.m.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the race on a Saturday?
For the first time in Baku's history, the F1 weekend will shift a day forwards, with the race taking place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijan National Day of mourning on the Sunday.

Azerbaijan's people will dedicate their thoughts to military personnel and those who died during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.

Baku City Circuit

After the European leg of the calendar where circuits are more traditional, Baku is one of the standout street circuits of the season.

The first race in Baku was held in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before it was called the Azerbaijan Grand Prix a year later.

The section around Turns 8, 9 and 10 are lined by the walls of the city's charming old town including a castle and the long main straight along the Baku shoreline sees cars reach speeds in excess of 220 mph and is the best spot for overtaking.

The walls are narrow and the high-speeds make for either a race full of chaos, or none at all. There is a 57% chance of a Safety Car being deployed during the race.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Circuit: Baku City Circuit; Baku, Azerbaijan

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2024: Oscar Piastri (McLaren)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2016 European GP. (First race as Azerbaijan GP in 2017)

Laps: 51 laps of 6km.

Lap record: 1:43.009, Charles Leclerc (2019).

Most wins: Pérez (2021, 2023) and Verstappen (2022, 2025) with two wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2018), Bottas (2019) and Piastri (2024).

Most poles: Leclerc with four (2021-2024) and Hamilton (2017), Bottas (2019) and Verstappen (2025) are the other pole sitters from the current grid.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be dry and sunny throughout the weekend. Temperatures will be around 26°C, but will drop to 24°C for the race on Saturday.

What happened last year?
Red Bull's Verstappen took pole position around the streets of Baku in a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags.

He ended up converting that pole into a dominant victory, with Russell in second and Carlos Sainz behind.

It was a key moment in the championship fight between Lando Norris and Piastri as Norris closed the gap to 25 points to his McLaren teammate after the Australian crashed out.

Who will win this year?

The last street circuit this year was in Monaco in June and since then several of the top teams have upgraded its packages and haven't yet gone racing on street circuits, but Baku has now arrived.

Antonelli has looked on fire in the last two races, but Norris is creeping to the front. The reigning world champion has two wins to his name in Hungary and Zandvoort, but also suffered an unlucky run in Madrid with the safety car deployment, so missed out on a potential win there as well.

Mercedes are set to be quick in the high-speed straight lines in Baku, but the tight and twisty corners might suit Ferrari and McLaren best.

One of the main aims will be to not crash the car into the wall otherwise the whole course of the race can rapidly change in a blink of an eye.

stories.headline: Paige Bueckers scores 25, Jessica Shepard secures another triple-double and Wings beat Storm 103-91
stories.summary: — Paige Bueckers scored 25 points, Jessica Shepard had 20 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists for her WNBA-leading sixth triple-double of the season, and the Dallas Wings beat the Seattle Storm 103-91 on Wednesday night in the regular-season finale for...
stories.body:
SEATTLE -- — Paige Bueckers scored 25 points, Jessica Shepard had 20 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists for her WNBA-leading sixth triple-double of the season, and the Dallas Wings beat the Seattle Storm 103-91 on Wednesday night in the regular-season finale for both teams.


Dallas (27-16), which won just 10 games last season, set a WNBA record for the best single-season turnaround in league history with a 17-win improvement. The Wings have won seven of their last eight games, with their lone loss coming on Monday after leading by 14 points.


Dallas led 90-71 with 6:55 left in the fourth quarter before Seattle went on a 17-4 run to get within 94-88. But Awak Kuier and Bueckers made 3-pointers on Dallas’ next two possessions to pull away.


Arike Ogunbowale added 23 points and six assists for Dallas, which secured the No. 7 seed in the WNBA playoffs after Atlanta’s victory over New York earlier in the night. Bueckers had 20-plus points and five-plus assists for the third straight game.


Dominique Malonga led Seattle (8-36) with 29 points and eight rebounds. Awa Fam scored a season-high 22 points, Flau’jae Johnson added 21 points, and Natisha Hiedeman had 10 points and 14 assists.


Dallas won all four games against Seattle this season to earn its first sweep over the Storm in franchise history.


Up next
Wings: Await playoff matchup.


Storm: Season is over.

Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Angus Crichton craves dream Roosters NRL farewell
stories.summary: Rugby-bound Sydney Roosters star Angus Crichton knows his NRL career is coming to a close and is desperate to go out with a bang.
stories.body:
Angus Crichton has placed the Rugby League World Cup on the backburner has he eyes a fairytale farewell from the NRL and Sydney Roosters.

Just one game into his comeback from foot surgery, Crichton claims he's not worthy of or fit enough for a place in Kevin Walters' 23-man Kangaroos squad for the October-November showpiece in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea.

"I'm just so focused on the next couple of weeks and obviously right now I'm battling with this foot," Crichton told AAP ahead of the Roosters' preliminary final with the Dolphins on Friday night.

"And if I'm being honest with you, there's back-rowers that are more deserving than me at the minute."

In reality, the 2025 Ashes tourist and 17-game NSW State of Origin stalwart would likely be among one of the first picked if he put his hand up.

But with Crichton heading to the NSW Waratahs at season's end, the 30-year-old would need a special exemption from Rugby Australia to even be considered for the World Cup, which ends on November 15.

Crichton is due to report for Waratahs duty on November 7 or in mid-October to RA if Wallabies coach Les Kiss wants the former Australian schoolboys star to travel with Australia A for two matches in the USA.

Little wonder Crichton is focused solely on the Roosters and his ongoing recovery after being out longer than he initially hoped.

"Three months is a long time to be sitting there on the sidelines watching the boys. It's been a long process. I'm glad to finally be back," said Crichton, who is thankful his first son, Sullivan, came in April.

"It was actually, it was a blessing in a way to have a bit of a distraction there because I've got a pretty busy mind at the best of times.

"So when you've got a lot more time on your hands, there's some tough moments."

After 212 NRL games, including 157 for the Roosters since joining in 2019, Crichton is intent on bowing out with a bang.

"It's all or nothing for us," he said.

"We just got to focus on this next game and everything that goes into it and just getting our bodies right and our minds in the right place to be primed.

"For me, it's 12 weeks post-op and the foot's still sore and it's been a tough road. But doing that role off the bench, the adrenaline gets into you and and you can make it work."

Crichton isn't the only Rooster leaving for the Waratahs. He will be linking with Roosters assistant Michael Cheika, who is returning to Daceyville 13 years after coaching the Tahs to their still one and only Super Rugby title.

"We don't talk about it," Crichton said of the elephant in the Roosters' dressing room.

"Obviously we both know that that's going to be happening and that'll be great, but right now we're just focused on the job at hand."

The 11-Test star and 2019 premiership winner isn't completely ruling out an NRL comeback after his two-season stint in rugby, which he hopes will include next year's World Cup in Australia.

"I'm always open to returning here but I'm pretty all in. If I'm doing something, I'm having a solid crack at," Crichton said.

"Right down the track, I could potentially come back to the league but the way I'm viewing this is this is my last couple of games of my NRL career and I'm looking to begin a new career."
